newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Guoco says will retain Centennial shares.
newsitem.headline: Guoco says will retain Centennial shares.

text.p: Guoco Holdings (Phlilippines) Inc said on Thursday it has no intention to sell its stake in Centennial City Inc.
"Guoco Holdings ... has no intention to sell its shareholdings in CCI," the company said in a statement.
Guoco owns 1.5 billion shares of the company's outstanding four billion shares.
Trading in Centennial shares was suspended on Wednesday for possible violation of full disclosure rules in connection with a 750-hectare reclamation project being undertaken along Manila Bay.
The award was given to the Amari consortium in which Centennial holds 20 percent, while Ital-Thai Public Development Plc is the other major stockholder.
The contract was questioned by a senator saying that the contract was underpriced. The Amari consortium denied any wrongdoing.
"All shareholders remain confident about the integrity of its Manila Bay developent project and remain committed to see the project to its final fruition," Guoco said.
Guoco is part of Guoco Holdings Ltd of Hong Kong.
In a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) hearing earlier in the day, Centennial City said it did not withhold any information regarding the contract.
The SEC, however, did not lift its suspension order, saying it needed written statement by major shareholders that they would not divest their shares.
Centennial shares have been falling in the past two weeks, closing at 2.80 pesos on Wednesday from 4.40 pesos per share on November 29.
